page.layout: One column of running text, with three stanzas of Latin verse set in italic in the lower half. Below the text: the signature "B 3" at left and the catchword "O uiua" at right. Running head centred above the text, page number at top right.

main_text.p: uidet[?] fuisse Prophetarum & Apostolorum, & aliorum Dei seruorum: ita, si se malis exosum, uenenatæ linguæ spiculis peti uideat, seipsum exhilarare debet. Turpe enim foret, iftis placuisse: honorificum, di splicuisse. Præstat Therfitas habere hostes & accusatores, quàm defensores.

Nonò, det operam, ut ex coniunctione dulcissima cum paucis, sed bonis, fructus consolationis, qui à συμφωνίᾳ fidei proficiscuntur, percipiat. Etsi autem illi plerumque sunt calamitosi & miserabiles: quia tamen in Christi nauicula sunt, cum iis periclitari, tutissimum & optimum fuerit. Noti sunt uersus Philippi Melanchthonis de Naui Christi, quæ est Ecclesia, digni quos ad unguem teneamus.

p.i: Auricomum uellus postquam transfuexit Iason In patriam, sperans debita regna sibi, Oppressit dominum nauis de culmine lapsa.
Sed quia defessus iam cubat ipse domi: Non te Christe tamē tua, quà regis, opprimet Argo Quamuis & rimis est lacerata suis.
Tum quoq; cum fluctus ciet imo ex gurgite Orion, Et rapidi uenti prælia sæua cient, Quassatam medio in pelago tua dextera seruat, Et uere es Nautis anchora sacra tuis.

page.notes: The first word of the page is partly cut off at the left edge; "uidet" is read with doubt because the first letter looks like an n. The Greek word "συμφωνίᾳ" is read with some doubt. The ampersand in "Quamuis & rimis" is taken to be "&" as printed. The reading "Iason" comes from the printed long s ("Iafon"). The catchword "O uiua" is read at the foot right, with some doubt about its last letters.
